optimization_notes: optimized.py: the two `for triple in helper(...): graph.add(triple)` loops are merged into one loop over the concatenation of the two lists the helpers return. Nothing else: the rights triple is guarded by `if rights_iri is not None`, and the first two adds have no shared-subject form in rdflib.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `graph = Graph()` and its designation become one `@graph as graph` (the fresh graph additionally carries the block's dct binding, record ldpy/027; the driver compares by isomorphism); the type/title pair becomes one `+{ ... ; ... }`; the guarded rights add becomes +{ } inside its if; URIRef(x) becomes f<{x}> (no @base), Literal(title) the bare {title}.

The merged helper loop stays `graph.add(triple)` on both sides: the triples arrive assembled by out-of-region helpers, and `for s, p, o in ...: +{ {s} {p} {o} }` would be longer without saying anything.
No exception to the symmetry rule.
